name: A Tipsy Charlotte
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ oz. Cooper's gelatine, soaked in a cup of cold water two hours

ingredients.name: 1 teaspoonful vanilla or bitter almond extract

ingredients.quantityText: 1 teaspoonful vanilla or bitter almond extract

instructions.text: Heat the cream almost to boiling; put in the soaked gelatine and half a cup of sugar, and stir until dissolved
Remove from the fire, flavor, and when cool, beat or churn to a standing froth
Cut off the top of the cake in one piece, and scoop out the middle, leaving the sides and bottom three-quarters of an inch thick
Over the inside of these pour the wine in spoonfuls, that all may be evenly moistened
Fill with the whipped cream, replace the top, which should also be moistened with wine and set in a cold place until needed
Serve with it, or pour around it, a custard made of the eggs, milk, and the other half cup of sugar

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the cream almost to boiling; put in the soaked gelatine and half a cup of sugar, and stir until dissolved
2. Remove from the fire, flavor, and when cool, beat or churn to a standing froth
3. Cut off the top of the cake in one piece, and scoop out the middle, leaving the sides and bottom three-quarters of an inch thick
4. Over the inside of these pour the wine in spoonfuls, that all may be evenly moistened
5. Fill with the whipped cream, replace the top, which should also be moistened with wine and set in a cold place until needed
6. Serve with it, or pour around it, a custard made of the eggs, milk, and the other half cup of sugar
